visualReview.observations: Full CP1 connector and all port-bank labels fit the desktop canvas. The selection toolbar crosses a middle divider but does not obscure contacts.
The CP3 checkbox and 256-cell badge agree; the edited ORG 255 draft, loaded cell 255, six displays and thirty key faces are visible. The two React-version images are byte-identical.

At 390 pixels the German dark panel displays all six digits and thirty key faces; CPU actions and text wrap. The source listing uses its contained horizontal scroll region. The two React-version images are byte-identical.
The complete trainer and attached circuit are visible. The exact incomplete draft and ROM identity are restored, while the CPU controls and keypad remain disabled without imported firmware.
The corrected fitted trainer is fully visible, including the right CP3 banks. All eight switch controls and the eight LED channels are visible.
The complete CP1 face fits the 390-pixel circuit overview. After normal inner-pane scrolling, all S1-S8 controls are visible and legible. The CP1 front panel and its wrapped actions fit below.

limitations: This is an actual-component integration browser suite in authored shells; production GUI menus and the complete Scratch VM were not exercised.
Known-monitor CP1 semantic stepping was not exercised in these browsers; synthetic firmware is correctly shown as unqualified for command debugging.
At 390 pixels the circuit is an overview requiring zoom for small schematic labels, and the small generic voltage legend remains partly clipped at the canvas right edge.

previousRuns.failure: Panel loader used a named Chromium export from a dynamically imported resolved CommonJS Playwright file; no panel browser launch
previousRuns.fix: Use the explicitly supplied Playwright CommonJS registry API

failures.cause: Immediate assertion raced the asynchronous React commit after switching fixture input ownership to circuit
failures.evidence: Failure screenshot already shows manual input checkboxes removed
failures.fix: Wait for actual checkbox detachment, retain the zero-count assertion

failures.cause: Fixture restored storage through low-level extraction without the normal project's load notification
completedChecks: Actual circuit button through CPU to LED
SB3 incomplete-source save with ROM identity only
failures.fix: Use production loadProjectFile with explicit minimal VM delegate and verify normal load announcement

failures.cause: Broad fixture PropTypes alias rewrote React16's development prop-types/checkPropTypes subpath
failures.fix: Exact package alias preserves React16's genuine internal subpath; development dependency optimizer preflight passed

failures.cause: A check() call assumed immediate checked state while the fixture intentionally held the asynchronous CP3 request
failures.fix: Click and verify pending disabled/unapplied state, then resolve and wait for the applied checked state

failures.cause: Actual React16 SyntheticKeyboardEvent lacks code: keydown ownership keyboard:4 did not match native keyup ownership keyboard:Digit4
failures.fix: Shared keyboard-owner helper reads nativeEvent.code when the synthetic code field is absent

failures.cause: Assertion read CPU time before scheduled single-step execution completed
failures.fix: Wait for observed instruction time advance and paused state, then retain exact shared clock-delta assertions

failures.cause: Actual CP1 footprint was the generic 48x48 fallback while rendered artwork is 300×400
failures.fix: Supplier CP1 footprint corrected to 300×400 with rotated/mirrored fit regressions; browser now requires rendered face containment after Fit

cp5.review: Functional switch/firmware/LED and pause tests passed. Screenshot inspection found the CP1 face clipped, so this run does not establish complete geometry qualification.
